01 / THE BIG IDEA

Your imagination.
The next playable thing.

Build Day is a friendly, self-paced game-making challenge for Roblox players. Each day has one achievable milestone, with short tutorials, tips, and examples to help you keep moving.

Work alone or with a small team. No previous building experience is required—just a Roblox account, access to Roblox Studio, and a willingness to try.

04 / A NOTE FOR PARENTS

Play is the spark.
Creating is the skill.

Build Day channels an interest in games into a hands-on creative project. The proposed activities make room for planning, logical thinking, experimentation, and learning from feedback.

✓

Creativity with a purpose
Make choices, solve problems, and build something original.

✓

Confidence through progress
Break a big idea into small steps and improve through practice.

✓

Flexible by design
Short resources and optional stretch goals keep the week manageable.

Good questions. Clear answers.

Does my child need building experience?+
No. The event starts with beginner activities and a small goal. Participants can work alone or in a small team, and unfinished but playable projects are welcome.
How does self-paced support work?+
Daily pages should include a short tutorial, screenshots or captions, a plain-language checklist, and an optional stretch. Participants never need to stay online continuously or attend a large live session.
How will a large online event stay safe?+
Use moderated announcements, clear community rules, no public sharing of personal information, team spaces with limited permissions, and a simple way to report concerns. [Safeguarding lead, reporting route, and supervision details TBC.]
How will the event stay accessible?+
Publish plain-language instructions, captions or transcripts, keyboard-friendly pages, high-contrast examples, downloadable resources, flexible deadlines during the week, and an offline-friendly checklist. [Specific accommodations and contact TBC.]

Showcase format[Date, platform, moderation plan, and viewing access TBC]

Feedback can be celebratory and specific: one delightful detail, one clever idea, and one next-step suggestion. Competition and prizes are optional and should never define success.
